sections.title: How to approach a coding interview
sections.intro_md:
```
 1. Clarify     inputs, outputs, constraints (n up to?), duplicates? negatives? empty? sorted?
 2. Examples    walk 1 normal + 2 edge cases by hand
 3. Brute force state it + its complexity (shows you understand the problem)
 4. Optimise    which pattern removes the repeated work? (see map below)
 5. Code        clean names, helper functions, no premature cleverness
 6. Test        run through your examples, then edge cases (empty, one item, all same, large)
 7. Complexity  time AND space, explain why
```

**Constraint → expected complexity:**
| n | Acceptable |
|---|---|
| ≤ 20 | O(2ⁿ), O(n!) backtracking |
| ≤ 10³ | O(n²) |
| ≤ 10⁵–10⁶ | O(n log n) or O(n) |
| ≥ 10⁸ / streaming | O(n) single pass, O(1)/O(log n) memory, or distributed |

questions.title: How do you analyse time and space complexity?
questions.short_md: Count how the number of operations grows with input size n, keep the dominant term, drop constants. Space = extra memory beyond the input (include recursion stack).
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** Count how the number of operations grows with input size n, keep the dominant term, drop constants. Space = extra memory beyond the input (include recursion stack).

| Big-O | Example |
|---|---|
| O(1) | dict lookup, list append |
| O(log n) | binary search, heap push/pop |
| O(n) | single loop, `x in list` |
| O(n log n) | sorting |
| O(n²) | nested loops over n |
| O(2ⁿ) | all subsets |

**Python costs to know:** `list.append/pop()` O(1) amortised; `list.insert(0,x)` / `pop(0)` O(n) → use `deque`; `x in set/dict` O(1) avg; `x in list` O(n); slicing `a[i:j]` O(j−i) copy; string `+=` in loop can be O(n²) → `"".join(parts)`; `sorted` O(n log n).

questions.title: What is amortised complexity?
questions.short_md: Average cost per operation over a sequence, even if some operations are expensive. A Python list over-allocates; occasionally `append` copies everything (O(n)), but averaged over many appends it's O(1).
questions.body_md: **Short answer:** Average cost per operation over a sequence, even if some operations are expensive. A Python list over-allocates; occasionally `append` copies everything (O(n)), but averaged over many appends it's O(1).

questions.title: Two Sum (classic hash-map problem)
questions.short_md: **Idea:** for each number, check whether its complement was seen before. One pass, O(n) time, O(n) space (brute force O(n²)).
questions.body_md:
**Idea:** for each number, check whether its complement was seen before. One pass, O(n) time, O(n) space (brute force O(n²)).

```python
def two_sum(nums: list[int], target: int) -> list[int]:
    seen = {}                                   # value -> index
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        if target - x in seen:
            return [seen[target - x], i]
        seen[x] = i
    return []
# two_sum([2, 7, 11, 15], 9) -> [0, 1]
```

questions.title: Two pointers
questions.short_md: **When:** sorted input, pairs, reversing, removing duplicates in place, palindromes.
questions.body_md:
**When:** sorted input, pairs, reversing, removing duplicates in place, palindromes.

```python
def pair_sum_sorted(nums: list[int], target: int) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums) - 1
    while lo < hi:
        s = nums[lo] + nums[hi]
        if s == target: return lo, hi
        if s < target: lo += 1        # need bigger sum
        else: hi -= 1                 # need smaller sum
    return None                       # O(n) time, O(1) space

def is_palindrome(s: str) -> bool:
    t = [c.lower() for c in s if c.isalnum()]
    return t == t[::-1]
```

questions.title: Sliding window
questions.short_md: **When:** best contiguous subarray/substring under a condition. Expand right; shrink left while the window is invalid.
questions.body_md:
**When:** best contiguous subarray/substring under a condition. Expand right; shrink left while the window is invalid.

```python
def longest_unique_substring(s: str) -> int:
    last = {}                        # char -> last index
    left = best = 0
    for right, ch in enumerate(s):
        if ch in last and last[ch] >= left:
            left = last[ch] + 1      # shrink past the duplicate
        last[ch] = right
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best                      # "abcabcbb" -> 3, O(n)

def max_sum_k(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:          # fixed-size window
    window = sum(nums[:k]); best = window
    for i in range(k, len(nums)):
        window += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
        best = max(best, window)
    return best
```

questions.title: Prefix sums
questions.short_md: **When:** many range-sum queries, or count subarrays with sum = k.
questions.body_md:
**When:** many range-sum queries, or count subarrays with sum = k.

```python
from itertools import accumulate
prefix = [0, *accumulate(nums)]               # prefix[i] = sum(nums[:i])
range_sum = lambda i, j: prefix[j + 1] - prefix[i]   # O(1) per query

def subarray_sum_equals_k(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    count, running = 0, 0
    seen = {0: 1}                             # prefix sum -> occurrences
    for x in nums:
        running += x
        count += seen.get(running - k, 0)     # earlier prefix that makes a sum of k
        seen[running] = seen.get(running, 0) + 1
    return count                              # O(n); works with negatives (window doesn't)
```

questions.title: Binary search (and its invariant)
questions.short_md: **Invariant:** the answer always stays inside `[lo, hi]`. Also used on an **answer space** ("minimum capacity to ship in D days").
questions.body_md:
**Invariant:** the answer always stays inside `[lo, hi]`. Also used on an **answer space** ("minimum capacity to ship in D days").

```python
def first_ge(nums: list[int], target: int) -> int:
    """Index of first element >= target (len(nums) if none). Same as bisect_left."""
    lo, hi = 0, len(nums)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if nums[mid] < target: lo = mid + 1
        else: hi = mid
    return lo

def min_capacity(weights: list[int], days: int) -> int:
    def ok(cap):                                  # can we ship within `days`?
        need, load = 1, 0
        for w in weights:
            if load + w > cap: need, load = need + 1, 0
            load += w
        return need <= days
    lo, hi = max(weights), sum(weights)
    while lo < hi:
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if ok(mid): hi = mid
        else: lo = mid + 1
    return lo
```
`import bisect` gives `bisect_left/bisect_right/insort`.

questions.title: Sorting — when is it the right tool?
questions.short_md: Python's `sort` is **Timsort**-derived (since 3.11 its merge order uses **Powersort**): O(n log n) worst, O(n) on nearly sorted data, **stable**. Sorting often turns a hard problem into a scan (intervals, dedupe, closest pairs). Custom order with `key=`.
questions.body_md:
Python's `sort` is **Timsort**-derived (since 3.11 its merge order uses **Powersort**): O(n log n) worst, O(n) on nearly sorted data, **stable**. Sorting often turns a hard problem into a scan (intervals, dedupe, closest pairs). Custom order with `key=`.

```python

```

questions.short_md: def merge(intervals: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]: intervals.sort(key=lambda x: x[0]) merged = [] for start, end in intervals: if merged and start <= merged[-1][1]: merged[-1][1] = max(merged[-1][1], end)   # overlap → extend else: merged.append([start, end]) return merged                                      # [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10]] -> [[1,6],[8,10]]

questions.title: Stack vs queue vs deque
questions.short_md: Stack = LIFO (`list.append/pop`); Queue = FIFO (`collections.deque.append/popleft`, O(1)); Deque = both ends O(1). `queue.Queue` is thread-safe (for producer/consumer threads); `asyncio.Queue` for coroutines.

questions.title: Monotonic stack
questions.short_md: **When:** "next greater/smaller element", stock span, largest rectangle. Keep the stack increasing/decreasing; each element pushed/popped once → O(n).
questions.body_md:
**When:** "next greater/smaller element", stock span, largest rectangle. Keep the stack increasing/decreasing; each element pushed/popped once → O(n).

```python
def next_greater(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    res = [-1] * len(nums)
    stack = []                                   # indices with decreasing values
    for i, x in enumerate(nums):
        while stack and nums[stack[-1]] < x:
            res[stack.pop()] = x                 # x is the next greater for that index
        stack.append(i)
    return res                                   # [2,1,2,4,3] -> [4,2,4,-1,-1]
```

questions.short_md: Detect a cycle (Floyd), find the middle, k-th from end.

```python
def has_cycle(head):
    slow = fast = head
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow, fast = slow.next, fast.next.next
        if slow is fast: return True
    return False
```

questions.title: Tree traversals
questions.short_md: class TreeNode: def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None): self.val, self.left, self.right = val, left, right
questions.body_md:
```python
class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None): self.val, self.left, self.right = val, left, right

def inorder(root):                       # left, node, right → sorted order for a BST
    return inorder(root.left) + [root.val] + inorder(root.right) if root else []

from collections import deque
def level_order(root):                   # BFS by levels
    if not root: return []
    out, q = [], deque([root])
    while q:
        level = []
        for _ in range(len(q)):
            n = q.popleft(); level.append(n.val)
            if n.left: q.append(n.left)
            if n.right: q.append(n.right)
        out.append(level)
    return out
```
Preorder (node first — copy/serialise), postorder (children first — delete, compute heights).

questions.short_md: def max_depth(root): return 1 + max(max_depth(root.left), max_depth(root.right)) if root else 0

```python
def max_depth(root): return 1 + max(max_depth(root.left), max_depth(root.right)) if root else 0

def is_bst(root, lo=float("-inf"), hi=float("inf")):
    if not root: return True
    if not (lo < root.val < hi): return False
```

questions.title: BFS and DFS
questions.short_md: **BFS** explores level by level (queue) → shortest path in **unweighted** graphs. **DFS** goes deep (stack/recursion) → components, cycle detection, paths. Both O(V + E).

questions.title: Cycle detection in a directed graph
questions.short_md: DFS with three colours: white (unvisited), grey (on current path), black (done). Reaching a **grey** node = back edge = cycle. (Or Kahn's algorithm: if topological sort can't include all nodes, there's a cycle.)

questions.title: Topological sort (Kahn's algorithm)
questions.short_md: **When:** order tasks with dependencies (build steps, course prerequisites, workflow DAGs — like Terraform's graph or `needs:` in CI).
questions.body_md:
**When:** order tasks with dependencies (build steps, course prerequisites, workflow DAGs — like Terraform's graph or `needs:` in CI).

```python
from collections import deque, defaultdict
def topo_order(n: int, edges: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> list[int]:
    indeg, adj = [0] * n, defaultdict(list)
    for a, b in edges:                    # a must come before b
        adj[a].append(b); indeg[b] += 1
    q = deque(i for i in range(n) if indeg[i] == 0)
    order = []
    while q:
        u = q.popleft(); order.append(u)
        for v in adj[u]:
            indeg[v] -= 1
            if indeg[v] == 0: q.append(v)
    return order if len(order) == n else []   # [] → cycle exists
```

questions.title: Dijkstra's algorithm
questions.short_md: **When:** shortest path with **non-negative** weights. Min-heap of (distance, node). O((V + E) log V). Negative weights → Bellman-Ford.

questions.title: Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union)
questions.short_md: **When:** grouping/connectivity queries, merging duplicates, Kruskal's MST. With path compression + union by rank, operations are ~O(1) (inverse Ackermann).
questions.body_md:
**When:** grouping/connectivity queries, merging duplicates, Kruskal's MST. With path compression + union by rank, operations are ~O(1) (inverse Ackermann).

```python
class DSU:
    def __init__(self, n): self.parent, self.rank = list(range(n)), [0] * n
    def find(self, x):
        while self.parent[x] != x:
            self.parent[x] = self.parent[self.parent[x]]   # path compression (halving)
            x = self.parent[x]
        return x
    def union(self, a, b):
        ra, rb = self.find(a), self.find(b)
        if ra == rb: return False
        if self.rank[ra] < self.rank[rb]: ra, rb = rb, ra
        self.parent[rb] = ra
        self.rank[ra] += self.rank[ra] == self.rank[rb]
        return True
```

questions.title: Dynamic programming — how to think about it
questions.short_md: DP = recursion + **memoisation** of overlapping subproblems (or bottom-up table). Steps: (1) define the **state** (what does `dp[i]` mean?), (2) **transition** (how dp[i] depends on smaller states), (3) **base cases**, (4) order of computation, (5) answer location, (6) optimise space.

questions.title: Longest increasing subsequence in O(n log n)
questions.short_md: Keep `tails[k]` = smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length k+1; binary-search where each number goes.
questions.body_md:
Keep `tails[k]` = smallest possible tail of an increasing subsequence of length k+1; binary-search where each number goes.

```python
from bisect import bisect_left
def lis(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    tails = []
    for x in nums:
        i = bisect_left(tails, x)
        if i == len(tails): tails.append(x)
        else: tails[i] = x
    return len(tails)               # [10,9,2,5,3,7,101,18] -> 4
```

questions.short_md: Greedy picks the locally best choice (interval scheduling by earliest end, coin change with canonical coins) — must be provably correct. If a counterexample exists (coins [1,3,4], amount 6: greedy 4+1+1=3 coins, optimal 3+3=2), use DP.

questions.title: LRU cache — implementation and complexity
questions.short_md: **Requirement:** `get` and `put` in O(1), evict the least recently used. Hash map (key → node) + doubly linked list (recency order). In Python, `OrderedDict` provides both.
questions.body_md:
**Requirement:** `get` and `put` in O(1), evict the least recently used. Hash map (key → node) + doubly linked list (recency order). In Python, `OrderedDict` provides both.

```python
from collections import OrderedDict
class LRUCache:
    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.cap, self.data = capacity, OrderedDict()
    def get(self, key):
        if key not in self.data: return -1
        self.data.move_to_end(key)              # mark as recently used
        return self.data[key]
    def put(self, key, value):
        self.data[key] = value
        self.data.move_to_end(key)
        if len(self.data) > self.cap:
            self.data.popitem(last=False)       # evict least recently used
```
Follow-ups: thread safety (lock), TTL expiry, `functools.lru_cache` for memoising functions, distributed cache (Redis `maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru`).

questions.title: Near-duplicate detection for 1M titles takes hours — what do you change?
questions.short_md: Pairwise comparison is O(n²) = 10¹² comparisons. Fix with **candidate generation**: normalise text → exact duplicates via hash set → near-duplicates via blocking (same first token / sorted tokens), **MinHash + LSH** (Jaccard similarity buckets) or **embeddings + ANN index** (FAISS/HNSW) to get top-k neighbours → then apply an expensive similarity (rapidfuzz, edit distance) only to candidates → union-find to group. Parallelise with multiprocessing; profile before tuning.

questions.title: Numeric overflow, precision and floats
questions.short_md: Python ints are arbitrary precision (no overflow). Floats are IEEE-754: `0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3` → compare with `math.isclose(a, b, rel_tol=1e-9)`; money → `decimal.Decimal` or integer cents; `fractions.Fraction` for exact ratios. NumPy ints **can** overflow.

questions.title: Rate limiter (coding version)
questions.short_md: import time, threading class TokenBucket: def __init__(self, rate: float, capacity: int): self.rate, self.capacity = rate, capacity self.tokens, self.updated = capacity, time.monotonic() self.lock = threading.Lock() def allow(self) -> bool: with self.lock: now = time.monotonic() self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + (now - self.updated) * self.rate) self.updated = now if self.tokens >= 1: self.tokens -= 1 return True return False
questions.body_md:
```python
import time, threading
class TokenBucket:
    def __init__(self, rate: float, capacity: int):
        self.rate, self.capacity = rate, capacity
        self.tokens, self.updated = capacity, time.monotonic()
        self.lock = threading.Lock()
    def allow(self) -> bool:
        with self.lock:
            now = time.monotonic()
            self.tokens = min(self.capacity, self.tokens + (now - self.updated) * self.rate)
            self.updated = now
            if self.tokens >= 1:
                self.tokens -= 1
                return True
            return False
```

questions.title: How would you find a race condition in concurrent Python code?
questions.short_md: Symptoms: wrong totals, intermittent failures. Look for shared mutable state accessed by multiple threads/coroutines with read-modify-write (`counter += 1`, check-then-act `if key not in d: d[key] = …`). Reproduce with stress tests (many threads, `sys.setswitchinterval` small), add logging with thread IDs; fix with locks, queues, atomic DB operations (conditional writes), or immutable data. In asyncio, races happen across `await` points (state changed while you awaited).
questions.body_md:
Symptoms: wrong totals, intermittent failures. Look for shared mutable state accessed by multiple threads/coroutines with read-modify-write (`counter += 1`, check-then-act `if key not in d: d[key] = …`). Reproduce with stress tests (many threads, `sys.setswitchinterval` small), add logging with thread IDs; fix with locks, queues, atomic DB operations (conditional writes), or immutable data. In asyncio, races happen across `await` points (state changed while you awaited).

```python
# check-then-act race in asyncio
if user_id not in cache:
    cache[user_id] = await fetch(user_id)   # two coroutines can both fetch; fine if idempotent,
                                            # otherwise use asyncio.Lock per key
```

questions.title: Sorting algorithms — which to know and why
questions.short_md: In real code use `sorted()` / `list.sort()` (Timsort-derived; since Python 3.11 the merge order uses **Powersort** — still **stable**, O(n log n), very fast on partly sorted data). In interviews, know how merge sort and quicksort work, their complexity, and stability.
questions.body_md:
**Short answer:** In real code use `sorted()` / `list.sort()` (Timsort-derived; since Python 3.11 the merge order uses **Powersort** — still **stable**, O(n log n), very fast on partly sorted data). In interviews, know how merge sort and quicksort work, their complexity, and stability.

| Algorithm | Average | Worst | Extra space | Stable | Key idea |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Merge sort | n log n | n log n | O(n) | yes | split in half, sort each, merge |
| Quicksort | n log n | n² (bad pivots) | O(log n) | no | partition around a pivot |
| Heap sort | n log n | n log n | O(1) | no | repeatedly pop max from a heap |
| Counting / bucket | n + k | n + k | O(k) | yes | small integer range |
| Insertion sort | n² | n² | O(1) | yes | great for tiny/nearly-sorted arrays |

```python
def merge_sort(a):
    if len(a) <= 1:
        return a
    mid = len(a) // 2
    left, right = merge_sort(a[:mid]), merge_sort(a[mid:])
    out, i, j = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
        if left[i] <= right[j]:          # <= keeps it stable
            out.append(left[i]); i += 1
        else:
            out.append(right[j]); j += 1
    return out + left[i:] + right[j:]

def quicksort(a):
    if len(a) <= 1:
        return a
    pivot = a[len(a) // 2]
    return (quicksort([x for x in a if x < pivot])
            + [x for x in a if x == pivot]
            + quicksort([x for x in a if x > pivot]))
```
**Stability** matters when sorting by multiple keys: sort by date, then (stable) by priority → items with equal priority stay in date order. Python: `sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r.priority, r.date))` does both at once.

questions.title: Bit manipulation basics
questions.short_md: from functools import reduce from operator import xor def single_number(nums):          # every number appears twice except one return reduce(xor, nums)      # O(n) time, O(1) space
questions.body_md:
| Trick | Code | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Check bit k | `(n >> k) & 1` | flags, permissions |
| Set / clear bit k | `n \| (1 << k)` / `n & ~(1 << k)` | flags |
| Is power of two | `n > 0 and n & (n - 1) == 0` | sizing |
| Count set bits | `n.bit_count()` (3.10+) | Hamming weight |
| XOR cancels pairs | `a ^ a = 0`, `a ^ 0 = a` | find the single non-duplicated number |

```python
from functools import reduce
from operator import xor
def single_number(nums):          # every number appears twice except one
    return reduce(xor, nums)      # O(n) time, O(1) space
```
Subsets via bitmask: for n items, numbers `0 .. 2**n - 1` enumerate every subset (bit i = item i included).

sections.title: Cheat sheet
sections.intro_md:
| Pattern | Template idea | Complexity |
|---|---|---|
| Sorting | Python = Timsort/Powersort, stable n log n; merge sort stable; quicksort n² worst |
| Bits | `n & (n-1) == 0` power of two; XOR cancels pairs |
| Grids | cells = graph nodes; BFS for shortest steps; multi-source BFS |
| Hash map | seen/complement/counts | O(n) |
| Two pointers | lo/hi move inward | O(n) |
| Sliding window | expand right, shrink left | O(n) |
| Prefix sum | `prefix[j+1]-prefix[i]`; sum-k with dict | O(n) |
| Binary search | invariant `[lo, hi)`; search answer space | O(log n) |
| Heap top-k | min-heap size k | O(n log k) |
| Monotonic stack | pop while violates order | O(n) |
| Intervals | sort by start, merge | O(n log n) |
| BFS | queue; shortest unweighted | O(V+E) |
| DFS | stack/recursion; components, cycles | O(V+E) |
| Topo sort | Kahn in-degree queue | O(V+E) |
| Dijkstra | min-heap of distances | O((V+E) log V) |
| Union-Find | path compression + rank | ~O(1) |
| Trie | dict of dicts | O(L) |
| Backtracking | choose, explore, un-choose | exponential |
| DP | state, transition, base, order | states × transition |
| LRU | OrderedDict / map + DLL | O(1) |
